To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
saccadic eye movement and slow eye drifts differentially activate neurons in V1.

saccadic and drift responses of V1 neurons are differentially affected by retinal image motion and position and that they are differentially modulated by extraretinal influences that may bias perception in favor saccade targets.

the visual responses of neurons in V1 are modulated by saccadic eye movement and that these modulations have different effects on the neuronal activity depending on the stimulus and eye movement parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural mechanisms of visual perception and cognition.
the neural basis of visual perception and cognition, and the neural mechanisms that underlie the generation of visual behavior, such as saccades, pursuit and fixation.
the neuronal mechanisms underlying perception of visual stimuli in the context of eye movements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the activity in V1 during saccades and drift can be explained as a combination of retinal and extraretinal effects.
the neuronal response to eye movements is not only stimulus driven, but also includes extraretinal influences.
the activity of V1 neurons is modulated in a complex and diverse way by saccades and by the retinal image motion generated by the saccades.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
saccades are the most important eye movements for visual perception.
the activity of V1 neurons is strongly affected by eye movements.
the activity of V1 cells can be modulated by saccades and by slow eye movements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain uses the information provided by eye movements in a highly efficient manner to improve perception of the visual world.
the brain has evolved to process visual information in an optimal way.
the activity of neurons in primary visual cortex can be modulated by eye movements in a number of ways.
